Visions and Values
Our vision and values are at the core of everything we do. They underpin our teaching and learning, and provide an environment which prepares our pupils as confident, happy citizens.
Success for today; prepared for tomorrow. Nothing is beyond our reach.
For children to operate as independent learners and thinkers
To inspire a love for learning
To provide a relevant curriculum for all
For children to value themselves
To foster a sense of belonging to a community
We believe that all of our communities have rights and choices. At The King Alfred Federation we promote the values of the Three R’s and the Three C’s.

Welcome
We are a busy and friendly school, with lots going on. This website aims to give you a taster of the school, as well as providing up to date information for parents, pupils and the wider community.
We hope that you enjoy your visit to our website, and that you find the information you are looking for. Please feel free to contact the school direct with any queries you may have.
A Message from Our Headteacher
Athelney Primary School is a unique and diverse learning community that provides the best possible support in enabling pupils to achieve their best. Pupils and staff are highly motivated and firmly believe in learning together, in partnership with families.
Children are at the centre of all we do at Athelney. Our curriculum is designed to foster curiosity and creativity, to develop motivation and habits that encourage our children to be life long learners. We are proud of the children who attend Athelney and expect them to aim for and achieve the best they possibly can. ‘Nothing is beyond our reach!’
Athelney is a fully inclusive school and we are incredibly proud of our outstanding Resource base for children with Autistic Spectrum Disorder which opened in 2010. Personalised learning across the whole school ensures we meet the needs of all children and enables them to reach their full potential. Children at Athelney feel safe, happy and achieve well.
As a successful school, we are committed to supporting and learning from others. Athelney Primary is federated with Elfrida Primary to form the King Alfred Federation. We are proud of our very successful federation and the opportunities that it opens up to children, staff and families.
We welcome visitors, so whether you are looking for a nursery/reception place or a professional looking for an inspirational setting to develop your career, please do not hesitate to contact us to arrange a visit.
Federation Headteacher
Athelney and Elfrida Primary Schools
The King Alfred Federation

Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club
Come and have a healthy start to your day!
At the King Alfred Federation, we want to encourage our pupils to be successful and as well-prepared for their school day as possible.
We offer a breakfast club facility that allows our pupils from Reception to Year 6 to have both a healthy breakfast and the chance to engage in play and activities before starting their school day.
What we offer at Athelney Primary School
Places must be booked in advance to ensure we have adequate staffing and can maintain a safe environment for all children. We are unable to accept children into Breakfast Club who have not been pre-registered.
You can book for as little as one day a week, or every day. Once a place is booked, it must be paid for - whether your child attends or not - as the space is reserved and cannot be offered to another child.
Payment must be made in advance.
If you are interested in your child joining then please download the below booking form and return to admin@athelney.lewisham.sch.uk. Alternatively, click here to book including ad-hoc booking.
Ad Hoc Bookings Available
We understand that families need flexibility. That’s why we also offer Ad Hoc Bookings: • £6.00 for a 7:30am drop-off • £5.00 for a 7:45am drop-off
Please confirm availability with the school office before making an ad hoc booking.
We are signed up to the Tax-Free Childcare vouchers!
Athelney Primary School is signed up to the Tax-Free Childcare for working families (including self-employed workers). Apply here and we will be able to accept the 20% towards your Breakfast Club bill.
After signing up, kindly inform the school office if you intend to use these to make payment for Breakfast Club.
We look forward to welcoming you in!

New Nursery Parents
Welcome to Rockets Nursery!
Pre-school education for 2, 3 and 4 year olds.
We want to wish a very warm welcome to Athelney Primary School to all of our new families. Here you will find important information for your child transitioning to Nursery, your child's teachers, ' A day in the life' and other useful information to support you and your child. Click on the subheadings below
In the meantime if you have any questions, queries, worries, ideas of things that would make this webpage better, please contact us through the office on 020 8697 2945 or email
Parents/Carers will often wonder what their child gets up to at nursery. Many parents/ carers collect their child and ask them what did you do today? / how was your day? and they will often get replies like 'it was good or I can't remember or I played'
So below is a little insight, for you, of your child's day - this shows a full timers day with morning and afternoon session
MORNING SESSION 8.45-9am: Settling in
I enter through the nursery gate Firhill road, where my parent/carer can come into the cloakroom to help me find my peg and hang up my belongings. It would be great if you can teach me here, how to take off my jacket and hang it up along with my bag- this helps me to become more independent. I then will find my name/photo to self register. I then will say goodbye to my parent/carer and begin doing some choosing time while waiting for my friends to arrive and before our first carpet session starts.
BUCKET TIME & PHONICS
Bucket Time is a fun, short group activity that helps me develop my attention and listening skills. During the session, the teacher uses a special "bucket" filled with exciting toys and activities to capture the my interest.
We are encouraged to:
Look and listen carefully.
Take turns and wait patiently.
Join in with simple activities.
Build my attention and concentration in a fun and enjoyable way.
Bucket Time helps me learn important skills I use every day, such as listening to instructions, focusing during group activities, and learning alongside others. Sessions are kept short, positive, and engaging so that I can experience success while having fun. We also add phonics, maths and art into this session too!
FREE LEARNING Learning through play is important part of of my nursery day. My classroom is designed to be accessible, engaging and fun for me to play, explore, and experiment independently, with my peers or with my teachers. There is a mixture of child led learning, adult guided learning and enhanced provision opportunities which will be linked to our learning for that week. We have a snack table which may have fruit, vegetables, bagels, cereal etc.. where I can help myself and learn to be independent. I am encouraged to help tidy up my classroom before the next carpet session, this helps me to become responsible for my own environment, show teamwork by working together with my friends, improves my understanding of following simple instructions, supports problem solving, language and strengthen my physical skills.
11.30-11.45am CARPET SESSION Singing and Literacy Story Our literacy story time is linked to Understanding of the world topic. I will listen to the story as we will talk about the story, my teacher will ask me questions and will get us to join in repeated refrains. Across the week there will be enhanced provision activities linked to this story.
11.45am Morning session is finished The children sit patiently on the carpet while the teacher calls their names. When their parent or carer arrives, they are called to collect their belongings from their peg before getting ready to go home.
11.45-12.30 LUNCHTIME
12.30-12.45 More children arrive through the Nursery Firhill gate for the afternoon session. They follow the same settling-in routine as the morning children, helping them to feel happy, confident, and ready for a fun afternoon of learning and play.
1.1-15pm BUCKET TIME & PHONICS
1.15-3 FREE LEARNING
Our full-time nursery children are collected at 3:00 pm.
When my parent or carer arrives, my teacher lets me know. I collect my jacket and belongings from my peg and get ready to go home. The rest of my class tidy up at 3pm.
3.15-3.30pm CARPET SESSION Singing and Literacy Story
3.30pm Afternoon session is finished The children sit patiently on the carpet while the teacher calls their names. When their parent or carer arrives, they are called to collect their belongings from their peg before getting ready to go home. You are welcome to collect your child earlier on Fridays, in line with the main school day. Friday collection 2.30pm.
Hopefully that shows you a lot about what I get up to at school so then you can ask me some targeted questions and hopefully I will give you more than 'It was good, I played or I can't remember?
Some questions you could ask me:
What exciting toys was in the bucket? Did you get to play with it? Did you do good waiting/ sitting? What sound do you think was in the box- what objects had the same sound?
What book did you read? What happened- can you tell me what you saw on the pictures?
Who did you play with? What did you do in your free learning time- what activities did you do? Did you sing a song? You looked like you done some great learning today- How did you get messy?

'Reading gave flight to my imagination and strengthened my understanding of the world, the society I lived in and myself'(Malory Blackman, OBE; Children's Laureate 2013-2015).
What are we doing to encourage a love of reading?
We share books with the children individually and a class text is chosen and shared with the entire class, by the end of the day .
How to READ with Your Child
Reading with your child at home will help them to succeed with their understanding of the world around them. It builds their vocabulary - therefore helping to improve their speech, their writing, Comprehension skills and empathy of others.
This is an important part of reading. Before the children become confident readers, they need to know how to match sounds to letters and then how to blend those sounds together to read words. Each morning, we practise recognising digraphs (two letters, one sound) and trigraphs (three letters, one sound) to support with reading and spelling words.
Tricky Words and Sight Words Song
Our writing is linked with our reading. Everyone is given the opportunity to listen to the class text. The children are then asked questions about the book, in order to check their comprehension and to correct any misunderstandings. They will then use what they understand to create different types of writing, in the form of:

Swimming - This is currently on pause and will resume again soon. We will notify you via email as soon as we have an exact start date.
PE - Currently on WEDNESDAYS with Coach Malachi, children must arrive to school wearing their FULL KITS: plain black shorts/leggings/tracksuit bottoms and a plain white t-shirt. No jewellery, including watches, to be worn for health and safety reasons.
Home Learning – Updated Fridays
Reading: Children can swap books in class when finished and will track their home reading on our class chart. We visit the school library every Friday, where they can borrow new books—please return them once finished! 😊
Home learning explained:
Spelling: Each Friday, children will bring home five personal ‘Common Exception Word’ spellings based on their assessments. We will have a test on Friday and any incorrect spellings will be repeated the following week. In addition to this, the Year 3 spelling rules are taught in class and can be practiced at home using EdShed, which offers five fun spelling games. Short, regular play sessions work best!
Number Facts: A highlighted number facts grid has been sent home, showing which facts your child is confident with. Practice these at home through flashcards, games or Times Table Rockstars, also best in short, regular bursts.

Special Interests
In the Resource Base we operate a special interest curriculum because we acknowledge that everyone learns best in the context of their own interests. So, when we are choosing texts for learning about writing or Science we consider an individuals interest. For example, if a pupil is interested in dinosaurs and fossils then we can tailor the activities to include researching, writing and math solving around dinosaurs.
Each Friday one pupil chooses the weeks interest based on their chosen topic. This gives one pupil the attention of all their peers for one special day and all learning activities are based on this particular interest. It's our favourite time of the week!
Thus far this term we have learnt about football, animals, ants and France/Japan.
Isla's Special Interest Friday... David Attenborough!
